# Command-line reference

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py; do not edit by hand. Regenerate with `make docs`. -->

The complete `initialize-claude-ai --help`. For what the options are for and how they
combine, see [Usage](usage.md) and the phase guides.

```text
usage: initialize-claude-ai [--config FILE] [--env-file FILE] [--set KEY=VALUE] [--secure]
                            [--do-cleanup | --no-cleanup] [--json] [--report FILE]
                            [--log-level LEVEL] [--log-file FILE | --no-log-file] [--quiet]
                            [--no-color] [-h] [--version]
                            {run,phases,config,palette,env} ...

Initialize a Claude AI environment: install, authenticate, provision, discover MCP.

positional arguments:
  {run,phases,config,palette,env}
    run                 run one or more phases
    phases              list the available phases
    config              show the effective configuration
    palette             preview the console colour schemes
    env                 show the environment initialize-claude-ai has recorded

options:
  -h, --help            show every option of every command, phase by phase, and exit
  --version             show program's version number and exit

configuration:
  --config FILE         extra TOML config file; repeatable, later files win
  --env-file FILE       dotenv file whose variables are loaded before settings are interpolated;
                        repeatable
  --set KEY=VALUE       override one setting, e.g. --set mcp.exhaustive=true
  --secure              refuse credentials given as values: only the --*-ref forms work, and an
                        inline literal: reference is rejected wherever it comes from

upkeep:
  --do-cleanup          at the end of the run, remove this program's own leftovers that nothing
                        uses -- its old temporary directories and unused work files (on by
                        default; run.cleanup)
  --no-cleanup          keep every leftover this run and earlier runs made

output:
  --json                print the JSON report on stdout and nothing else
  --report FILE         also write the JSON report to FILE
  --log-level LEVEL     console detail: trace, debug, info, warning or error (the log file keeps
                        logging.file_level)
  --log-file FILE       record this run in FILE instead of paths.log_file
  --no-log-file         do not record this run to a file at all
  --quiet               suppress the human-readable output; the log file and --report still record
                        the run
  --no-color            disable ANSI colour

=== initialize-claude-ai run: run one or more phases ===

Run the initialization phases in order: 1 install, 2 auth, 3 provision, 4 mcp. Every flag below is
shorthand for a setting, so anything given here can equally be put in a config file or an
environment variable. Exit status: 0 success, 1 a phase failed, 2 the command line was refused (or
a partial run, with run.partial_is_failure), 130 interrupted.

run control:
  Which phases run and how the run as a whole behaves, whichever phases those are.

  --phases LIST         phases to run: numbers, names, ranges or 'all' (default: all, from
                        run.default_phases)
  -n, --dry-run         simulate every change; read-only probes still run, so the report stays
                        truthful
  -a, --auto-agree      answer yes to every confirmation, for unattended runs
  --ignore-failure      run the remaining phases even after one fails (same as
                        run.continue_on_failure=true)
  --no-partial-success  stop when a phase is only partly successful, which by default is not fatal
  --timeout DURATION    wall-clock ceiling for the whole run: 45s, 90m, 2h, 1d or plain seconds.
                        It stops new work from starting; work already under way finishes, so the
                        run can overrun by one address. Addresses never reached are named in the
                        report, so list the important ones first. No ceiling by default; per-
                        operation timeouts are unchanged
  --timeout-scale FACTOR
                        multiply every per-operation timeout (5 s connects up to 30 min sign-ins)
                        by FACTOR, keeping their proportions: 2 doubles them, 0.5 halves them.
                        Default 1.0. Useful on a slow link or with --concurrency

any phase:
  Read by more than one phase; give them with whichever phases you run.

  --gcloud-project, --vertex-project ID
                        Google Cloud project for the whole run: phase 2 signs in against it and
                        points gcloud at it, phase 3 bills Vertex to it. Without it:
                        ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID, GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT or
                        CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT, then gcloud's active project
  --auth-anthropic-key-ref REF
                        Anthropic API key, sent as x-api-key, read from REF: env:NAME, file:PATH
                        or keyring:svc/user
  --auth-anthropic-key VALUE
                        Anthropic API key, sent as x-api-key, given as the value itself (visible
                        in ps; refused by --secure)

phase 1 (install) - Install the Claude AI toolchain:
  Verify, install and re-verify every catalog component -- the Claude Code CLI and whatever
  runtime, cloud CLI and MCP tooling the selected backend needs. These flags take effect only
  when the phase runs (--phases 1 or install).

  --install-only LIST   install only these components: comma-separated component keys or group
                        names (base, runtime, claude, cloud, browser, desktop, mcp-tooling, mcp-
                        runtimes); list them with 'initialize-claude-ai config components'
  --install-skip LIST   skip these components; same syntax as --install-only, and it wins over it
  --install-prefetch {none,launchers,all}
                        also install what phase 4 launches MCP servers with: 'launchers' the
                        programs behind install.demand_sources (npx, uvx, ...), 'all' every mcp-
                        runtimes toolchain (go, rust, deno, bun, docker) too, 'none' neither.
                        Optional; --install-only wins. Default: install.prefetch (launchers)
  --force-install       reinstall every selected component, even those that already verify
  --break-dependencies  let pip and uv install into a PEP 668 externally managed Python (--break-
                        system-packages)
  --downgrade           install the known-good releases pinned in install.pins instead of the
                        latest

phase 2 (auth) - Authenticate:
  Sign in to each selected backend -- Google Cloud, claude.ai and the Anthropic API -- in two
  passes: detect what credentials already exist, then acquire only the missing ones. These flags
  take effect only when the phase runs (--phases 2 or auth).

  --auth-backend LIST   credentials to obtain, comma separated: google-cloud (what Vertex reads),
                        claude-oauth (the claude.ai session), anthropic-api, or 'all' (the
                        default)
  --force-auth          sign in again even where a working credential was found; the existing one
                        is still reported, and is not removed
  --force-auth-with-reset
                        --force-auth, after clearing the existing credentials: revoke the gcloud
                        login and application-default credential, log the claude CLI out, and
                        empty this program's own browser profile. Your own browser stays signed
                        in; the sign-in says how to get one that asks. Confirms first; destructive
                        and host-wide
  --headless            you open the URL yourself: every backend prints a URL -- no browser is
                        opened -- and waits for the code the page shows. Without it the code is
                        pasted back too, and the URL is opened for you where a browser can be
                        shown
  --browser-loopback-redirect
                        redirect sign-in (opt-in): every backend opens a browser that hands the
                        result back to this machine by itself, with no code to fall back on if it
                        never arrives. Not with --headless
  --browser COMMAND     command that opens a URL, %s standing for it ("firefox %s"). Default: the
                        first known browser on PATH. Opens the sign-in URL, and is exported as
                        BROWSER for sign-ins that open it themselves
  --browser-input-fix WHEN
                        give the browser GTK's built-in input method: auto|always|never. Use
                        'always' if what you type into the sign-in form vanishes when the field
                        loses focus
  --browser-profile WHEN
                        sign in with a browser profile of this program's own: auto|always|never.
                        No extensions, no earlier sign-in. A reset turns 'auto' into 'always'
  --sign-in-capture WHEN
                        capture the printed sign-in URL whole into a file and the clipboard, so a
                        wrapped URL never has to be selected: auto|always|never. 'never' gives the
                        sign-in your terminal directly
  --gcloud-user-account EMAIL
                        Google account gcloud must be signed in as; any other active account
                        counts as not signed in, so phase 2 signs in again
  --gcloud-service-account EMAIL
                        impersonate this service account from the signed-in user, with no key
                        file; not with --gcloud-service-account-file
  --gcloud-service-account-file PATH
                        sign in as the service account whose key JSON is at PATH; gcloud reads the
                        file itself, so the key never passes through this program
  --claude-user-account EMAIL
                        claude.ai account this machine should be signed in as; named in the sign-
                        in prompt, and a mismatch is warned about
  --auth-anthropic-token-ref REF
                        Anthropic bearer token for gateways and proxies, sent as Authorization,
                        read from REF: env:NAME, file:PATH or keyring:svc/user
  --auth-anthropic-token VALUE
                        Anthropic bearer token for gateways and proxies, sent as Authorization,
                        given as the value itself (visible in ps; refused by --secure)
  --auth-claude-token-ref REF
                        long-lived Claude Code OAuth token, read from REF: env:NAME, file:PATH or
                        keyring:svc/user
  --auth-claude-token VALUE
                        long-lived Claude Code OAuth token, given as the value itself (visible in
                        ps; refused by --secure)

phase 3 (provision) - Provision & configure:
  Choose the backend Claude Code talks to, resolve the account, project and region behind it,
  ask that backend which models it will actually serve, and write the result into settings.json
  and the environment files. These flags take effect only when the phase runs (--phases 3 or
  provision).

  --provision-backend NAME
                        API Claude Code is configured against: vertex, anthropic-api, bedrock or
                        auto (the default)
  --use-vertex 0|1      allow Vertex at all (1, the default); 0 leaves it out of 'auto' and
                        refuses --provision-backend vertex
  --gcloud-region NAME  Vertex location, e.g. us-east5. 'global' (the default), 'us' and 'europe'
                        are multi-region
  --default-model TIER  tier Claude Code starts on: opus, sonnet or haiku (a model id is accepted
                        and mapped to its tier). Written as settings.json "model". Default:
                        provision.default_tier (opus)
  --default-opus-model ID
                        pin the opus tier to this model id instead of the best opus the backend's
                        catalogue offers
  --default-sonnet-model ID
                        pin the sonnet tier to this model id instead of the best sonnet the
                        backend's catalogue offers
  --default-haiku-model ID
                        pin the haiku tier to this model id instead of the best haiku the
                        backend's catalogue offers

phase 4 (mcp) - MCP auto-discovery:
  For each address given to --mcp-server, work through the stages until one settles it: existing
  endpoint, published package, generated bridge, then strategy. These flags take effect only
  when the phase runs (--phases 4 or mcp).

  --mcp-server LIST     servers to find an MCP endpoint for, comma separated and repeatable,
                        written however you have them (example.com, https://api.example.com/mcp,
                        localhost:3000); each is normalised to one base URL first
  --mcp-recheck LIST    prove these addresses again after acting on the report: only their
                        existing and last working entries are tried, with the usage checks and
                        repairs -- nothing is searched for. Written like --mcp-server; 'all' re-
                        checks every entry of the project file (e.g. a .mcp.json copied from
                        another machine)
  --stages LIST         stages to try, in order, comma separated: endpoint, package, bridge,
                        strategy (default: all)
  --concurrency [N]     work N addresses at once; bare --concurrency uses
                        mcp.discovery.target_concurrency_bare. Shortens the wait, not the work or
                        tokens; output stays in address order. Default: one at a time
  --mcp-provision-missing {auto,always,never}
                        when a candidate needs a program that is not installed (go, cargo, uvx,
                        ...), install it from the phase 1 catalog, once per run: 'auto' only
                        without a password prompt, 'always' privileged strategies too, 'never'
                        reject it as before. Never changes which server is chosen. Default:
                        mcp.packages.provision_missing (auto)
  --mcp-trust-ca FILE[,FILE]
                        extra certificate authorities (PEM) to trust for every probe, registered
                        stdio server and generated bridge in this run, for targets behind an
                        internal CA. Node needs the self-signed root, not only an intermediate.
                        Default: mcp.trust.extra_ca (none)
  --mcp-trust-pin {targets,never}
                        when a target's certificate is not trusted here, 'targets' learns the
                        chain it presents (addresses you asked for only; kept under
                        mcp.trust.store_dir and reported with its fingerprint), 'never' does not.
                        Default: mcp.trust.pin_presented_chain (targets)
  --exhaustive-mcp      register every working MCP endpoint per address, not just the first: runs
                        every stage and probes every candidate path. Slower; not with --the-best-
                        mcp
  --the-best-mcp        search widely, score what answers (function, ease, setup, stability,
                        security, protocol, provenance) and register only the best per address.
                        Weights: [mcp.ranking]; not with --exhaustive-mcp
  --no-reuse-existing-mcp
                        do not offer servers already registered here (.mcp.json, `claude mcp
                        list`) as candidates for the address they point at. Default:
                        mcp.discovery.reuse_existing (true)
  --no-agent            traditional mode: deterministic probing and rule-based reasoning, no
                        Claude subagent. Same stages and report; an unusual server is likelier to
                        go unfound. --agent-max-turns and --agent-max-attempts then have no effect
  --agent-max-turns N   turn budget for every phase-4 subagent, replacing each stage's own. Lower
                        makes a run cheaper; raising it usually wants --timeout-scale too. At
                        least 1; default: each stage's own
  --agent-max-attempts N
                        tries the phase-4 agent gets per stage, each told what went wrong with the
                        last (= --set mcp.agent.max_attempts=N). Transient failures are not
                        counted. At least 1; default: mcp.agent.max_attempts
  --mcp-token-ref REF   bearer token used when probing an MCP target, read from REF: env:NAME,
                        file:PATH or keyring:svc/user
  --mcp-token VALUE     bearer token used when probing an MCP target, given as the value itself
                        (visible in ps; refused by --secure)

=== initialize-claude-ai phases: list the available phases ===

List the registered phases, their numbers and whether each is enabled.

=== initialize-claude-ai config: show the effective configuration ===

Print the configuration after every layer has been merged and every ${VAR} interpolated.
Credentials are redacted. Exits 1 if KEY is not set.

positional arguments:
  key  dotted key or subtree to print, e.g. provision.vertex.region; omit for the whole document

=== initialize-claude-ai palette: preview the console colour schemes ===

Print every colour scheme as a swatch, plain and bold, so the choice can be made by eye. Set the
winner with --set console.palette=NAME, INITIALIZE_CLAUDE_AI_CONSOLE_PALETTE, or console.palette
in a config file.

=== initialize-claude-ai env: show the environment initialize-claude-ai has recorded ===

Print the binary paths and versions phase 1 recorded, plus the line to source so this shell can
see them.

examples:
  initialize-claude-ai run --dry-run
  initialize-claude-ai run --phases 1 --install-only claude-cli,gcloud
  initialize-claude-ai run --phases 2 --auth-backend google-cloud --headless
  initialize-claude-ai run --phases 2 --gcloud-user-account me@example.com --force-auth
  initialize-claude-ai run --phases 2 --auth-backend google-cloud --force-auth-with-reset
  initialize-claude-ai run --phases 3 --provision-backend vertex --gcloud-region us-east5
  initialize-claude-ai run --phases 4 --mcp-server example.com,https://api.example.com
  initialize-claude-ai run --phases 4 --mcp-server example.com --exhaustive-mcp
  initialize-claude-ai run --phases 4 --mcp-recheck example.com
  initialize-claude-ai run --phases 4 --mcp-server example.com --the-best-mcp
  initialize-claude-ai run --phases 4 --mcp-server example.com --no-agent
  initialize-claude-ai run --phases 4 --mcp-server a.example,b.example --concurrency 2
  initialize-claude-ai run --phases 4 --mcp-server example.com --agent-max-attempts 5
  initialize-claude-ai run --secure --auth-anthropic-key-ref keyring:anthropic/prod

'run' may be left out when the first argument is an option:
  initialize-claude-ai --dry-run   is the same as   initialize-claude-ai run --dry-run
```
